clue.text: Country house from which a veil is lifted

definitions.meaning: the Marchmain family seat in Evelyn Waugh's novel ... Revisited

definitions.text: from which a veil is lifted
definitions.meaning: read literally, a ..., uncovered when the veil is raised at a wedding

explanation.surface: A stately home is unveiled to the public, as if at a grand opening.
explanation.walkthrough: BRIDESHEAD is the house in Evelyn Waugh's novel Brideshead Revisited; split, it is BRIDE'S HEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The title estate of Waugh's novel is the best-known fictional English stately home.

clue.text: Having abandoned evil, curse withdrawn

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters are scattered loose

explanation.surface: Someone gives up cursing and retreats into silence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having abandoned' looks like giving up the words, but 'abandoned' is the anagram signal for EVIL and CURSE together.
explanation.definitionFit: A shy hermit who shuns company is unsociable and retiring.

clue.text: Take steps to secure copyright in Hamlet, say

indicators.note: to secure means to hold fast, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: Hamlet was Prince of Denmark, so he is an example of a Dane
C is the abbreviation for copyright, as in the circled C symbol

explanation.surface: Someone acts to protect the rights to Shakespeare's play.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet looks like the play but is the Danish prince, so 'say' marks him as an example of a DANE.
explanation.definitionFit: To move the feet in rhythm to music is to step or trip.

clue.text: Well, well — bishop captured in game

indicators.note: captured in means one piece is caught between the others

parts.note: a spring is a well or natural source of water
OK means fine or well
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A surprised exclamation as a chess bishop is taken mid-game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' suggests chess but means hunted animals; 'Well, well' gives two different synonyms.
explanation.definitionFit: A southern African gazelle is a wild animal hunted for sport, which is what game means.

clue.text: Uplifting volume I have found thrilling

indicators.note: in a down clue, uplifting means the word is raised so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: a tome is a large volume or book
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A reader finds an inspiring book gripping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uplifting' turns TOME upwards to make EMOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Stirring or moving language arouses strong feeling.

clue.text: Initial appearance of daughter on TV's upsetting

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees

indicators.note: upsetting in a down clue means overturning a word so it reads upwards

parts.note: the tube is slang for television; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A girl's first TV performance proves distressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' turns TUBE upwards into EBUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A first public performance or launch is someone's opening show.

clue.text: Where boats can moor in island sound

indicators.note: sound here means a spoken version, so a word is taken as said aloud

parts.note: a key is a low island or reef, as in the Florida Keys

explanation.surface: A mooring spot in a channel of water off an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like a stretch of water beside the island, but it signals that KEY is heard as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A wharf or landing stage is built for vessels to tie up alongside.

clue.text: Sort of 3 seen as being exercise with energy

parts.note: qua is Latin-derived English for 'in the capacity of' or 'as being'
a drill is a training exercise
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A form of dance is regarded as a workout needing vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 refers to the answer at 3-down, DANCE. QUA is a formal word for 'as being'.
explanation.definitionFit: A square dance for four couples is a type of ballroom step.

clue.text: Helps maybe fence in area with stakes

parts.note: stakes are bets or wagers

explanation.surface: A garden fence is put up with posts in the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: A fence is a receiver of stolen goods, so 'maybe fence' points to a criminal who is helped; stakes are wagers, not posts.
explanation.definitionFit: To aid a wrongdoer, perhaps a receiver of stolen goods, is to assist in crime.

clue.text: Race is on to develop summary of plot

indicators.note: to develop means these letters grow into a new form, a rearranging of them

explanation.surface: A runner hears the race is about to start and imagines how it will unfold.
explanation.definitionFit: An outline of a film or play's storyline is a synopsis of how events will run.

clue.text: Trail this coat as pioneer

parts.note: put 'trail' before this jacket and you get a word for a pioneer who marks a new path

explanation.surface: An invitation to drag one's jacket about like an explorer.
explanation.walkthrough: To trail one's coat is to provoke a quarrel, which hides the real reading: TRAIL plus the coat makes a word for a pioneer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports or club jacket is a classic coat, and prefixed with trail it names an innovator.

clue.text: Go round holding extremely expensive dish

indicators.note: holding means one piece clasps the other within it

parts.note: to go round is to turn

indicators.note: extremely points to the extreme letters, the first and last of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone passes round a costly serving vessel at dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives the first and last letters of 'expensive', E and E, which go inside TURN.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep lidded bowl for serving soup is a piece of tableware.

clue.text: Profit from midwinter break

indicators.note: from tells us a run of letters is lifted out of the word that follows

parts.note: a break is a rest

explanation.surface: Someone earns money during the winter holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes INTE out of 'midwinter'; 'break' is a pause, REST.
explanation.definitionFit: Money earned on a loan or deposit is a return or gain.

clue.text: Come first to grand part of house

parts.note: to come first in a contest is to win
G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: A winner is promised a grand part of a house as a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: An extension built off the main block of a mansion is a section of it.

clue.text: Rumours from here horribly enrage VIP

indicators.note: horribly suggests these letters are mangled into another order

explanation.surface: Gossip makes an important person furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horribly' rearranges ENRAGE and VIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearing something on the grapevine means picking it up as unofficial gossip.

clue.text: After flight descent, one might call for porter here

definitions.text: After flight descent, one might call for porter here

parts.words: After flight descent, one might call for porter here
parts.note: a flight is a staircase going down, and porter is a dark beer, so this is an underground store for drink

explanation.surface: An air traveller, just landed, shouts for someone to carry the bags.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a plane landing and a baggage porter, but the flight is stairs and porter is a dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: An underground room where ale and stout are kept is reached by going downstairs.

clue.text: Showing details of land record, including area belonging to stars

indicators.note: including means the first piece takes the second inside it

parts.note: a CD is a compact disc, a kind of record
astral means relating to the stars

explanation.surface: A star chart turns up in a land register.
explanation.walkthrough: 'land record' looks like a single phrase, but 'record' is the start of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A register of property boundaries and ownership is a cadastre, and this adjective relates to one.

clue.text: Habit died, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: in means the first-named piece goes inside the others

parts.note: diction is a manner of speaking or enunciation
D is the abbreviation for died in genealogy

explanation.surface: A habit died out, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a manner of speaking' looks like an idiom; it splits into the insertion signal 'in', A and DICTION.
explanation.definitionFit: A dependency, such as one on drugs, is a compulsive habit.

clue.text: Did some more boxing, as English forwards rampaged around

indicators.note: around means the first piece wraps round the next ones

parts.note: to rampage is to rage
in rugby, the forwards are collectively the pack

explanation.surface: English rugby forwards run riot, boxing on as if in a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxing' suggests fighting, but it means putting things into boxes again; the rugby pack is the English forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To put goods into fresh cartons is to box or wrap them again.

clue.text: Having eaten nothing, Cook needs a large animal

indicators.note: having eaten means the first piece has swallowed the second

parts.note: to grill is to cook under direct heat
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A chef who has eaten nothing needs a big beast to roast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' seems to be a chef but is the verb, GRILL.
explanation.definitionFit: The biggest of the great apes is a heavyweight primate.

clue.text: American religious leader's current movement

definitions.meaning: the founder of Christian Science, Mary Baker of New Hampshire, known by her third husband's surname
a swirling of water or air against the main flow

explanation.surface: A US preacher's latest campaign is gathering pace.
explanation.walkthrough: Mary Baker EDDY founded the Christian Science church in Boston in 1879.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary Baker Eddy founded the Christian Science church, and a whirlpool is a circling current.

clue.text: Craftsman's derisive effort skilfully covered up

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: covered up means the outer piece hides the next piece inside it

parts.note: a jeer is a mocking cry
to do something skilfully is to do it well

explanation.surface: An artisan's scornful attempt was cleverly hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: A maker of rings and necklaces is a skilled worker in gems and precious metals.

clue.text: Celebrate as old charge is reduced

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: is reduced means the word loses a letter from its end

parts.note: a toll is a charge for using a road or bridge

explanation.surface: Someone celebrates when an old fee is lowered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is reduced' cuts the last L off TOLL.
explanation.definitionFit: To praise someone highly is to laud or glorify them.

clue.text: Is in van, we hear, in city

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word is judged by how it is spoken

parts.note: to be in the van, the front of a column, is to lead

explanation.surface: Someone is travelling in a van through the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'van' is the vanguard, the front, not a vehicle. LEEDS is a large city in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeds is a major city in West Yorkshire, northern England.

clue.text: Only catching a cold? That's a relief

indicators.note: catching means the outer word traps the others inside

parts.note: sole means only, as in sole survivor
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone is relieved it is just a cold they have caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catching' in the surface is catching an illness; here SOLE catches A and C.
explanation.definitionFit: Comfort in distress is consolation, an easing of grief.

clue.text: Scientific invention upset old Royal Society to its core

indicators.note: to its core means the next piece goes into the middle of the first
upset in a down clue means overturned, so the word reads from the bottom up

parts.note: real is an archaic word for royal, surviving in real tennis

explanation.surface: A new device shocks the venerable Royal Society deeply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns REAL into LAER, and 'to its core' puts S in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A device emitting an intense narrow beam of light was a landmark of 1960s physics.

clue.text: Great bowling, but it's hit

definitions.meaning: in tenpin bowling, knocking all ten pins down with the first ball
to land a blow on someone

explanation.surface: A bowler's terrific delivery strikes home.
explanation.definitionFit: Toppling every pin with one ball scores top marks, and to smack or punch is the second sense.

clue.text: Authority informed on test situation

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means the first-named piece is placed after the second

parts.note: LORD'S is the London ground where Test cricket matches are played
hip, like hep, is slang for well informed or in the know

explanation.surface: An official is told about the venue for an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: LORD'S is a cricket ground in London that stages Test matches, which is why it is a 'test situation'.
explanation.definitionFit: The rank of a peer carries dominion and power over an estate.

clue.text: Such ice is said to behave like water

indicators.note: is said means a word is spoken and its sound is what counts

parts.note: water's behaviour is to run or flow

explanation.surface: A remark that ice will melt and run like water.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheet of sea ice drifting on the water is a typical polar form.

clue.text: Run round shopping centre to get details of contract

indicators.note: round means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: to sprint is to run fast
a mall is an indoor shopping centre

explanation.surface: Someone races round a mall to collect a contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shopping centre' is not a hint for a word's middle letters; it is simply a mall.
explanation.definitionFit: The fine print of an agreement holds the conditions and clauses that are easily missed.
